question: What is the main focus of health economics in a healthcare system?

options.A: Allocating scarce resources to meet population needs
options.B: Reducing the total number of nursing schools
options.D: Eliminating all diseases within a decade

explanation: Health economics looks at how limited resources are distributed to get the best health outcomes for the community. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is it important for Nigerian nurses to understand basic health economics?

options.A: Economic factors have no impact on daily nursing duties
options.B: Clinical outcomes depend entirely on international loans
options.C: Economic constraints directly affect bedside resource availability
options.D: Nurses are solely responsible for hospital budgeting

explanation: Financial decisions at the top trickle down and change the supplies, equipment, and staffing levels you see on the ward. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h1)

question: A weak national economy most directly leads to which result for public health institutions?

options.B: Immediate elimination of all user fees
options.C: Surplus medical equipment in rural clinics

explanation: When the national economy dips, government revenue drops, which leads to lower budgets for public health services. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why does currency devaluation heavily impact the cost of healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigeria imports most pharmaceuticals and medical devices
options.B: Nurses are paid exclusively in foreign currency
options.C: International donors refuse to accept local currency
options.D: Local factories produce all necessary hospital equipment

explanation: Because most medical supplies come from outside the country, a weaker local currency makes buying essential goods much more expensive. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is a direct benefit of investing money into healthcare infrastructure?

options.A: Modernization of facilities and advanced diagnostic tools
options.B: Reduction in patient populations across all hospitals
options.C: Elimination of the need for nursing personnel
options.D: Complete eradication of chronic infectious diseases

explanation: Funding allows hospitals to upgrade their buildings and get modern medical technology. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h3)

question: How does improved information technology positively affect healthcare delivery?

options.A: It completely stops power outages in rural clinics
options.B: It replaces the role of physicians in diagnosis
options.C: It enables telemedicine and digital health monitoring
options.D: It removes the need for clinical documentation

explanation: Good tech systems make remote consultations possible and help track patient records digitally. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main reason many Nigerian nurses move to other countries to practice?

options.A: Excessive numbers of local nursing positions
options.B: Search for better remuneration and working conditions
options.D: A lack of interest in clinical practice locally

explanation: Economic challenges and low local pay often push healthcare workers to look for jobs abroad. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h4)

question: How does economic growth help solve national healthcare staff shortages?

options.A: By funding educational institutions and expanding training capacity
options.B: By replacing human staff with automated machinery
options.C: By banning international travel for health professionals
options.D: By lowering the educational requirements for licensing

explanation: With better funding, nursing and medical schools can admit more students and train enough professionals for the workforce. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h4)

question: What payment method pays for a large proportion of healthcare in Nigeria?
explanation: Because health insurance coverage is still low, most Nigerians pay for their medical care directly from their own pockets. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h5)

question: What happens when a patient delays seeking medical care during high inflation because their money went toward food instead?

options.B: Worsened disease prognosis and increased complication risks
options.D: Decreased burden on hospital nursing staff

explanation: Waiting to get help because of money issues usually means the illness gets worse, leading to harder health outcomes later. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h5)

question: How do economic recessions typically affect public hospital supplies and equipment?

options.A: Consumables are distributed free of charge to all patients
options.B: Supplies become overly abundant due to decreased patient volume
options.C: Supplies become scarce and equipment maintenance budgets are slashed
options.D: Equipment is upgraded to modern digital specifications

explanation: Economic downturns mean less money for hospitals, leading to a shortage of supplies and a lack of equipment repairs. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which challenge do nurses commonly face during severe economic downturns in hospitals?

options.A: Having surplus support staff for every shift
options.B: Experiencing reduced working hours and excessive rest
options.C: Receiving automatic salary increases to match inflation
options.D: Managing heavier patient loads with fewer resources

explanation: When hiring freezes happen and supplies drop, nurses have to care for more patients using fewer materials under high stress. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h6)

question: How are economic development and healthcare facilities generally distributed in Nigeria?

options.A: Complete absence of hospitals in major cities
options.B: Equal resource allocation across all rural areas

explanation: Most investments and advanced hospitals are concentrated in big cities rather than rural areas. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why do rural populations often experience worse health outcomes than city dwellers?

options.A: Long travel distances and a shortage of skilled health personnel
options.B: Immediate access to advanced diagnostic technology
options.C: Lower disease prevalence requiring less medical care
options.D: Excessive numbers of specialized private clinics

explanation: Rural areas deal with distance barriers, poor roads, and too few trained health workers. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of health insurance schemes in handling economic challenges?

options.A: Protecting households from catastrophic out-of-pocket spending
options.B: Increasing the cost of essential medications
options.C: Eliminating the need for any healthcare workers
options.D: Ensuring hospitals generate maximum commercial profit

explanation: Health insurance shares financial risks so families don't go broke paying for unexpected medical bills. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h8)

question: How do public-private partnerships help improve healthcare in developing countries?

options.A: By combining resources and expertise to bridge service delivery gaps
options.B: By making all healthcare services entirely free of charge
options.C: By stopping the importation of foreign medical equipment
options.D: By completely removing government oversight from hospitals

explanation: When government and private bodies team up, they pool money and management skills to improve healthcare delivery. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h8)
